newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 29.

text.p: Three prominent Auckland Maori leaders resigned on Tuesday as directors of Aotearoa Television Network, the Maori station given $4 million by the government to keep it afloat till the end of June. The directors said they did not want to become liable for any debts the company incurred. Meanwhile, Communications Minister Maurice Williamson said taxpayers could expect a bill "considerably" bigger than the $4 million committed to Aotearoa TV as the government moved to meet Treaty of Waitangi obligations to provide Maori television. Page 1.

NZ First had committed a "balls-up" in failing to file a return of its election campaign spending on time, president Doug Woolerton said on Tuesday. He said the party would provide the return in about a week. NZ First is the largest of several parties that have failed to notify the commission of their spending, despite returns being due last Thursday. Page 2.

Education Ministry confidence that schools would have enough teachers for the start of the school year was misplaced as far as one country town school was concerned, and probably for similar schools, principal Denis Cave said on Tuesday. Cave's

school, North Clyde Primary, in Wairoa, has two vacancies for teachers. On Tuesday he had two parents caring for one class and a teacher aide in another. Cave said he had been unable to attract suitable New Zealand-trained teachers. Page 2.

Coercion was commonly used for more than 30 years to force birth parents in New Zealand to give children up for adoption, according to Social Welfare Department post-election briefing papers. However, the department says calls for an inquiry into past adoption practices will not necessarily help those who had been hurt. Page 2.

Much lower interest costs and increased traffic levels helped Tranz Rail Holdings boost its December half-year profit by $5.2 million to $24.1 million. Company chairman Ed Burkhardt said Tranz Rail results continued to improve while the New Zealand showed modest growth. Interest and related costs fell by more than $7 million to $10.2 million for the latest six months, because of repayment of longterm debt after the company's initial public offering in June last year. Page 12.

Underground Fashions will disappear from the sharemarket after Australian retailer Just Jeans finishes mopping up shares in the company. Just Jeans struck a deal at the weekend to buy the 71.4 percent of Underground held by company founders Barry and Diane Rissetto provided it stood in the market for the rest of the shares at the same buyout price of 33.5 cents each. On Tuesday Just Jeans Holdings successfully bought 1 million of the 7.5 million shares it needs to reach full ownership of the clothing retailer as speculative trading slowed. Page 12.

ANZ Bank's new managing director in New Zealand is David Airey. A former chief of the Rural Bank in New Zealand, Airey will take up his new post as head of ANZ Bank in New Zealand on March 1 and move to Wellington soon after.

Consumer spending intentions dived in the December 1996 quarter despite unchanged overall consumer confidence, the latest WestpacTrust McDermott Miller confidence survey has found. A growing number of survey participants expected improved personal finances and better economic times in the next year, but those who felt now was a good time to buy a big household
item fell sharply to the lowest level since December 1990. Page 10.

New Zealand sold more goods overseas than it imported in December, achieving the first trade surplus for six months. The tiny surplus of $10.4 million came in the traditional start of the export trade season and compares with a $7.2 million surplus in December 1995. Economists said the figures were in line with expectations of a balance in the trade figures and therefore they had no impact on the financial markets. Page 13.

Pacific Retail would struggle to meet its pre-tax profit target for the year but was keen to consider expansion into Australia, managing director Greg Lancaster said. The company expected to more than double its pre-tax profit in 1997-98, despite the current tough trading conditions. But Pacific Retail, New Zealand's largest retailer of home appliances and consumer electronics, would struggle to post its forecast $7 million pre-tax profit for the 1996-97. Page 23.
